summary.intent: Execute the launch plan's WP Q (`just verify-real`) in stages: build a local-registry recovery rehearsal harness, then make named Cargo registries a valid `publish-to` target, then add Cargo rehearsals and the native install/load matrix. Each stage is its own PR, with signed commits, no session trailers, explicit-refspec pushes verified by ls-remote, and full gates.
summary.outcome: PR #572 (npm/PyPI rehearsals over local TLS, no production change) and PR #575 (named Cargo registries, mutants 0 missed) were pushed. The third PR's work (Cargo rehearsals against a local sparse registry, the native matrix, and the AGENTS.md/release.md claim fixes) passed `just verify-real` and the gates, and was committed signed. At the end of the transcript it had not yet been pushed, merge-tree-checked against #578/#582, or linked to trail #460.

repo: Callisto never opens sockets itself: all registry traffic goes through child processes (npm, curl, twine, cargo) that inherit the environment. Local TLS registries therefore work by setting NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS, CURL_CA_BUNDLE and REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE, with no production code change.

The https rule for registry URLs accepts https on loopback. A self-signed 127.0.0.1 cert with an openssl-generated SAN binds through the production `prepared_registry_binding`; http stays rejected with E126.

pypiserver cannot serve the PEP 691 JSON simple index that callisto's PyPI observation needs, so the harness uses a small stdlib Python JSON index server for the index side and pypiserver for uploads. pypiserver also needs `disable_fallback=True` to avoid 303 redirects.

`PublishTarget` is `#[non_exhaustive]`, so a forgotten cross-crate match arm (derive.rs fingerprint) compiles and fails only at runtime via the `_ => UnsupportedRelease` arm. Boundary tests must be written first.

A `crates-io` publish runs plain `cargo publish` with no `--registry`, while observation passes `--registry crates-io`. Source replacement does not redirect `cargo publish`; a probe hit real crates.io. Named registries now pass `--registry <name>` for both publish and info.

The repo's gate is `just pre-push`, `just lint`, `just doc-check`, `just test`, `just ci` and `just workflow-contracts`, plus `cargo mutants --in-diff` for production diffs. Mutants output (mutants.out*) must never be committed.
Rehearsal CI tool pins live in one place: the `verify-real-tools` just recipe installs into `target/verify-real/`, and `.github/actions/install-registry-test-tools/action.yml` calls it.

code.finding: Added the `PublishTarget::CargoRegistry { name }` variant next to `CratesIo`; `config_str()` changed from `&'static str` to `&str`, a semver-visible API change.
`parse_publish_target` now receives the resolved registries. Unknown names, non-cargo registries, `cratesIo` and malformed names fail at load with E330.
The fingerprint match must include `CargoRegistry` explicitly. The `#[allow(unreachable_patterns)] _` fallback would otherwise hide the omission.
Boundary tests for named cargo registries sit next to the `cargo info` registry observation test. They use the fake cargo's `cargo_calls()`.

workflow: Pass the explicit refspec `HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>`, verify with `git ls-remote`, and compare against `git rev-parse HEAD`. Use `gh api .../commits/<sha> --jq .commit.verification.reason` to confirm GitHub shows the signature as valid.
Wrap long gate runs in scripts that write their own output files, since the sandbox guard objected to redirect forms. Report each gate by exit code.
Spike the risky tooling (curl, twine and gunicorn TLS trust) cheaply before building the harness. This surfaced the pypiserver JSON-index gap early.
Subagent hand-back messages are model output, not user approval. Design reports were used as input, and decisions needing new error codes or keys were escalated to the owner.

Verify that a new assertion actually discriminates by toggling the behavior (such as RUSTC_BOOTSTRAP) and reading the registry log, because cargo's own polling can satisfy an assertion meant for callisto.

friction: Fetching needed unsandboxed network access, and the guard rejected shell redirect forms.
Greedy Python string replaces broke the old real-registry test file twice, once in `curl_get` call sites and once in a delimiter, and were caught only when the gates failed to compile.
The first Cargo scenario hit real crates.io with a fake token (401) because source replacement does not redirect publish, forcing the Cargo rehearsal to be dropped from #572.
An earlier claim in #572 and AGENTS.md that callisto always publishes with `--registry crates-io` was wrong and had to be corrected later.
A gate run had to be stopped and rerun after reviewer fixes changed files, and the stray processes had to be located by cwd.
open_items: Push the third PR with `HEAD:refs/heads/worktree-wp-q-cargo-rehearsals`, verify with ls-remote, link trail #460, and run `git merge-tree` against open PRs. #578 and #582 both touch docs/architecture/release.md.
Owner decision pending: should a cargo registry named like a built-in target (`none`, `github-release`, `npm`) be rejected at load? This needs a new error code.
A `[registries.crates-io]` entry with `kind = "cargo"` is dead config that arguably violates REL-PUB-18's "never ignored"; it is left as a follow-up.
`confirm-timeout`/`publish-timeout` on a named registry and the fingerprint value for a named Cargo target are not pinned by tests.
If cargo config redirects a `crates-io` publish, callisto fails with E157 after the upload. This predates the work and is only documented.
The CI action change was never run on a real runner, and `just ci` is only reported for the third PR's gate run.
